source.title: Unifying Grokking and Double Descent
source.authors: Xander Davies; Lauro Langosco; David Krueger

record.tranche_reason: It tests model-wise and epoch-wise double-descent-like behavior using transformer experiments on modular division, a different experimental setting from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own transformer results in Figures 4–7 and a constructed pattern-learning model in Figure 2. Results it attributes to Power et al. (2022) and other cited work are not recorded as this study’s findings.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own decoder-only transformers on division mod 97 and sweeps embedding dimension and training steps. It reports test loss and accuracy curves with the fall-rise-fall shape on both axes. This is a new setting (algorithmic task, grokking regime), with results bearing on V1 and V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that grokking and epoch-wise double descent are the same pattern-learning-speed dynamics, and that these dynamics transfer to model size. They present what they call the first demonstration of model-wise grokking (delayed generalization as width grows).
record.recipe_differences: Uses decoder-only transformers trained on division mod 97, varies embedding dimension and optimization steps, and measures loss and accuracy; it follows the cited grokking setup rather than reproducing the original double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-accuracy pattern is described as faint while the test-loss pattern is more pronounced; Figure 7 also identifies a special early-learning pattern in modular division.

fits_no_version.finding: A constructed three-pattern sigmoid model of pattern learning reproduces epoch-wise double-descent and grokking curves. The two are interpolated by changing the maximum predictiveness of the patterns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent and grokking can both arise from patterns learned at different speeds with different generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: In modular division, an early fast-learned pattern (0/b=0) briefly lifts test accuracy above chance before memorization drives it below chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The first test-performance bump in epoch-wise curves reflects a fast, well-generalizing heuristic pattern.

record.peer_reviewed: ML Safety Workshop, 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)
record.problems: The empirical evidence is limited to the stated modular-division transformer setting. Several plotted results are qualitative and provide no extractable numerical values or uncertainty estimates; the test-accuracy double-descent signal is described as faint.
record.rows_left_out: No own results bearing on tested versions were left out. Results cited from Power et al. (2022) and other related work were excluded.

untested.parts: Only transformers on division mod 97 with fixed weight decay 1e-5. No other tasks or architectures, and no label-noise variation.
The authors explicitly avoid committing to an effective-complexity metric. No prediction of peak location is tested.
No variation of label noise or regularization, and no test of multiple peaks.

missing.what: The authors' own replication run of Power et al. (epoch-wise). It shows a small double descent visible in log accuracy and a more pronounced one in test loss. It was wrongly excluded as a cited result.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The evidence is qualitative heatmaps and curves, with no numbers, seeds or uncertainty reported. Default model is 2 layers, width 128, trained 400K steps with AdamW, weight decay 1e-5. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because the method (width and step sweeps) is the original's, applied in a new algorithmic, grokking setting. The second descent here is grokking-like, occurring well past interpolation.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments test model-wise behavior in the stated modular-division setting, not across other model classes or tasks.
The experiments test epoch-wise behavior in the stated modular-division setting, not across other model classes or tasks.
The paper does not sweep training-set size to test whether more data raises test error near interpolation.
The paper does not empirically test double descent across model classes; its pattern-learning model is a proposed explanation, not such a comparison.
The paper says it avoids specifying a precise effective-complexity metric and does not test whether one measure predicts peak locations across axes.
The paper does not test noise-driven peaks, multiple descent peaks, or disappearance of peaks under optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not recast model complexity in effective parameter counts to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
